findings.explanation: HOL4 specifies dest_var only on Var. A single constructor-pattern clause goes through Prim_rec.new_recursive_definition (hol4/HOL4-src/src/tfl/src/Defn.sml:1192), which ends in new_specification of that equation alone, so dest_var on Const, Comb and Abs is unspecified. Lean returns the same ARB for all three constructors. It therefore proves dest_var (Const n ty) = dest_var (Comb s t), dest_var (Comb s t) = dest_var (Abs u v), dest_var (Const n ty) = dest_var (Const m ty'), and dest_var (Const n ty) = ARB. HOL4 leaves all of these open. Compare VARIANT_PRIMES in the same module, which is translated as an epsilon over its specification.
findings.repair:
def dest_var_spec (f : term → mlstring × type) : Prop := ∀ x ty, f (Var x ty) = (x, ty)

def dest_var : term → mlstring × type := Classical.epsilon dest_var_spec

@[simp] theorem dest_var_def : ∀ x ty, dest_var (Var x ty) = (x, ty) := by
  have h : dest_var_spec dest_var := by
    apply Classical.epsilon_spec (p := dest_var_spec)
    exact ⟨fun t => match t with | .Var x ty => (x, ty) | _ => default, fun _ _ => rfl⟩
  exact h
findings.lean_check:
import CandleLean.HolSyntax

namespace Candle

example (n : mlstring) (ty : type) (s t : term) : dest_var (term.Const n ty) = dest_var (term.Comb s t) := rfl

example (s t u v : term) : dest_var (term.Comb s t) = dest_var (term.Abs u v) := rfl

example (n m : mlstring) (ty ty' : type) : dest_var (term.Const n ty) = dest_var (term.Const m ty') := rfl

end Candle
findings.hol4_check: ?f:term -> mlstring # type. (!x ty. f (Var x ty) = (x,ty)) /\ (!n ty s t. f (Const n ty) <> f (Comb s t))
